plainTranslation: Complementary emotional opposites. One needs space where the other needs closeness; one processes aloud where the other goes quiet. Failure mode: each reading the other's style as rejection. Name your needs explicitly - the contrast can balance you once you stop taking it personally.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.

summaryDeep:
You may both want to feel safe, understood, and supported, but reach those feelings in completely different ways. One of you may want to talk things through immediately, while the other needs time before they know what they feel. One of you reaches for closeness when upset, while the other needs space before they can reconnect.

This can create a frustrating dynamic where both people are trying to care for each other, yet neither feels fully cared for. The problem is rarely a lack of love or effort. It is that each person instinctively offers the kind of comfort they would want themselves.

When this works, it becomes a lesson in emotional flexibility. You begin to see that support can take many forms. Someone needing space is not necessarily pulling away from you. Someone needing reassurance is not necessarily asking for too much. The relationship stretches both people beyond their usual habits and teaches them new ways of giving and receiving care.

The real challenge is assuming that your way is the right way. When your emotional needs become the standard, the other person can start to feel unseen, even when your intentions are good. Over time, both people may end up feeling misunderstood by someone who genuinely cares.

The opportunity here is learning to get curious instead of making assumptions. Ask what helps. Pay attention to what actually settles the other person rather than what would settle you. The more you learn each other's emotional language, the less time you spend missing each other and the more time you spend feeling truly understood.
